classification: All seven literal declarations are upstream and unchanged. The Hanlin adapters are not byte-identical upstream and have the two enforcement-scope differences below.

findings.summary: A single original 10-second value is applied across multiple Hanlin prepared source compilations.
findings.upstream: ScriptWidgetCompiler.compile creates deadline inside each invocation, original lines 342–350 and 407–416; original $import invokes transform again at 922–945.
findings.host: HanlinWidgetCompiler.swift 80–108 creates one immutable deadline before entry and reuses it for every import. prepare-widget.js 48–74 likewise shares that callback across module transforms.
findings.minimalProposal: Retain the original compileTimeout authority and cooperative guard, but scope the deadline to each original compiler/source operation rather than a whole Hanlin package preparation. Do not introduce a replacement package-wide timeout.

findings.summary: A single-element root Fragment is counted as an additional Hanlin element and level, while upstream unwraps it first at unchanged depth.
findings.upstream: Original resolveWidgetElementTree 776–810 unwraps only a root single-element Fragment (including nested child arrays) at unchanged depth, then validateElementTree 123–156 counts the normalized tree.
findings.host: HanlinScriptWidgetRuntime.swift 288–322 increments the budget before normalization and always freezes the Fragment child at depth + 1; there is no equivalent root unwrapping.
findings.sourceReasonedBoundaryCase: A single-element root Fragment wrapping a tree of 1,000 elements or depth 64 stays within the original limits after normalization, but the host counts 1,001 or depth 65. This case was not executed.
findings.minimalProposal: Mirror original single-root-Fragment normalization at each rendered/region root before charging the node budget or incrementing depth. Keep nested non-root Fragment behavior, component/array cycle errors and all seven original authority values.
